Regular meetings are held on the 4th Monday of every month.

Library at (626) 300-0777 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.

noticing each teleconference location from which a member will be participating in a public
meeting.

  CORONAVIRUS DISEASE (COVID-19) ADVISORY
As a precaution to protect both staff, our constituents, and elected officials, the City is
following the State of California Health Department’s guidance on large
gatherings. Therefore, this meeting will take place via teleconference. Members of the
public are encouraged to watch or listen to the meeting from home, or provide input
electronically.

Members of the public may observe and offer comment at this meeting telephonically or
otherwise electronically:

  1) Public comment will be accepted by email to imcdermott@cityofsanmarino.org
  before or during the meeting, prior to the close of public comment on an item, to
  be read by the Board Chair during public comment. Lengthy public comment may
  be summarized in the interest of time.

  1. PUBLIC INPUT SESSION REGARDING THE SAN MARINO CENTER
  RENOVATION PROJECT

  Chairperson Mollno requested that the minutes reflect the questions and comments
  discussed during the public input session for the San Marino Center Renovation Project.

  Community Development Director Aldo Cervantes provided the PowerPoint
  presentation for the renovation project.

  Guiding question for the renovation project: Why does the San Marino Center need to
  be renovated?
   Should the exterior architecture of the building remain 1950’s mid-century
  modern style or adopt Spanish styles to mimic the Crowell Public Library?
  o Responses are unanimous to Spanish style and the windows should match
  style of Library
  o Trustees conveyed concern that the proposed design of the Center is not
  child-friendly. The design should incorporate wet bars, hand washing
  stations, and restroom near the catering kitchen
   Should there be outdoor courtyards for outdoor activities?
  o Responses conveyed the desire for indoor/outdoor spaces to maximize
  outdoor areas especially during Covid-19 times
  o The Center cannot be physically connected to the Library since the
  buildings are on separate plots; however, the buildings can be brought
  closer to create a sense of harmony
   Should the landscaping be refreshing or match the Library?
  o The pickup area by the Library should be changed to be more open to
  connect with the Center. Trustees indicated that there should be more
  than just matching architectural style of the Library
   Should the meeting rooms be larger or smaller?
  o Responses stated that there must be a variety of sizes of rooms to
  accommodate the different needs of people
   Should the stage remain?
  o Trustees stated to ask what will be the function of the stage before deciding
  on its removal
   Is there anything else specific you would like to see improved for the Center?

SUBJECT:  CITY LIBRARIAN’S UPDATE REPORT FOR SEPTEMBER 2020

BACKGROUND

At the request of the Library Board of Trustees, the City Librarian provides a monthly update of
the operations of the Crowell Public Library of the City of San Marino. The update report
provides relevant statistics and information to allow the Board to have a macro view of the
Library.

DISCUSSION

Since the virtual Trustee meeting of August 24, 2020, the library has continued to provide
vigorous curbside checkout service. August circulation was up 8% over July’s.

Friends of the Library

The next meeting of the Friends of the Library will happen on Wednesday, September 30. They
plan to discuss their next contactless book sale.

San Marino Public Library Foundation

The San Marino Public Library Foundation met via Zoom on September 14. They discussed plans
for their 25th anniversary celebration and a path forward to establishing a planned giving program.

Operations

The timing of the lights and the HVAC in the library have been adjusted to be off on the nights
and the weekends.

Staff temperatures are taken daily to screen for employees who might be ill.

  9
 We will request that Michael Throne be present at our meeting on October 26 to further explain
library CIP projects.

In October, Youth Services Librarian Tera Torres will begin the picture book reorganization. She
will start small, organizing several popular subject “neighborhoods” such as transportation,
royalty and superheroes.

Virtual Art Gallery; On the library home page, there is a link to a video of a walk-through of Justin
Mattock’s exhibit, which is still hanging.

Since the last Trustee meeting, there have been no changes in the status of COVID 19 in the City
or the County. The library will not open until after September 30. However, passport collections
resumed on September 1, 2020 outside of the Friends Bookshop.

Statistics

Statistics show that our total circulation, administered through curbside pickup, rose 8% from
July. Our e-Book circulation went down slightly from the previous month, dropping 7%.
Reference staff answered 77 queries in August, a 79% increase from July.

In the first three weeks of September, the library accepted 78 passport applications.

Programming and Services

We have heard complaints that our open hours, Monday through Friday from 11-4, are
inconvenient for working people. We propose shifting our open hours to 2 p.m. – 7 p.m. on
Thursdays.

During the week of September 15 – 21, the library hosted an obstacle course outlined in chalk
on West Drive. This was to encourage library-adjacent physical activity

September is Library Card Sign-up month. Children who posted a picture of themselves with
their Crowell Library card, wrote why they love the library, and tagged @crowellpubliclibrary
were entered to win a $25 gift card to Vroman’s Bookstore.

Virtual programming for the fall includes live Zoom Bingo for children, a YA Slime tutorial and
the new Crowell Book Club in November and December.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the Library Board of Trustee receive and file this information report.

SUBJECT:  MANAGEMENT ANALYST’S UPDATE REPORT

BACKGROUND

At the request of the Library Board of Trustees, the Management Analyst provides a monthly
update of the financial condition of the Crowell Public Library of the City of San Marino. The
update report provides relevant information to allow the Board to have a macro view of the fiscal
health of the Library. In addition, the report includes information about projects funded through
the Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) and other major assignments overseen by the Management
Analyst.

DISCUSSION

FY 20-21 Budget Update – August 2020 Summary

The Library continued to maintain its conservative spending habits in response to the
uncertainties stemming from Covid-19. Overall, spending dropped in personnel and in operational
expenditures in comparison to July. The Library received $355.66 in General Fund revenues and
revenues are expected to increase due to passport collections having resumed in September.
Aside from lower-than-expected revenues, the Library continues to maintain its strong financial
health by remaining within its budgetary limits.

In addition, the Library did receive a $20 donation to use towards Adult Chinese Materials and
continued to not spend out of Restricted Donations. To reiterate the Board’s direction, the
Library will not spend from the Restricted Donations accounts until there is more clarity from
Covid-19 and the fiscal impacts to the Library. Lastly, attached to this report is the City’s
Donation Policy that guides the City’s actions as it relates to receiving and expending from
donated monies.

  14
 Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) Projects

Per the Board’s direction, staff will seek reauthorization of CIP funding from Council for the
Barth Room Audio/Visual upgrade. This request will be reviewed on Friday, September 25, 2020.

Public Works is in communication with the Planning & Building Department to install a bottle-
watering station in the Crowell Public Library. A walk-through was held on August 20, 2020 and
Public Works is developing the Scope of Work. A completion date for this project has not yet
been determined.

Preliminary planning for the window-tinting project is underway. Due to the project’s anticipated
cost, three informal bids will be required before any installations may occur. A completion date
for this project has not yet been determined.

Public Works is working to finalize a schedule for the City’s sidewalk repair projects and has not
yet determined when work at the Library will begin.

Other Items

The City Council approved the Board’s request to change their minutes to a summary format as
opposed to an action format. The change in format is effective for any Board minutes taken after
the date of Council approval. As such, the minutes of the Board’s September 28, 2020 meeting
will be the first to be written in a summary format.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the Library Board of Trustees receive and file this information report.

 TO:  Josette Espinosa, Interim Community Services Director
FROM:  Paul Chung, Finance Director

DATE:  August 24, 2020
SUBJECT:  LIBRARY REVENUES IN RESPONSE TO COVID-19

The City’s budget process began February 2020 and the proposed budget was drafted in May
2020. In order to generate the operating budget for the library, the budget analysis was conducted
with the assumption that the library was going to be operational by July 2020. Obviously, the
library didn’t open in July and continues to be closed in the near future.

As you are aware, library operational costs are heavily covered by the City’s General Fund. This
isn’t unique to San Marino. Libraries aren’t revenue generating as they are a service provided to
the community using tax dollars. Crowell library’s revenues for FY 2020-21 is $183,086, if you
net out Passport Fees of $164,086, revenues from library operations is $19,000 or 10% of the
total library revenues. The library’s FY 2020-21 operating expenditures are $1.6M, the cost
recovery through library revenues is less than 12%.

As COVID-19 closures continue to impact the library from opening up and bringing in revenues,
the City and the Trustee should look at alternative funding options. Options could be potentially
furloughing staff, terminating staff, providing virtual classes, and continuing passport processing
while maintaining social distancing.

I am aware of the concern of the Trustees regarding the continual closure of the library and the
fiscal impact. If library operations continue to be closed, I would need to reevaluate the library’s
FY 2020-21 operating budget and make recommendations of possibly furloughing staff or other
cost cutting measures with the City Manager. This will happen during the fall, during FY 2020-21
mid-year review, where I will analyze the overall financial condition of the City, the impacts due
to COVID-19, and make a recommendation to the City Council for a mid-year update to the
City’s operating budget. Best business practices are to wait 5-6 months before making budget
adjustments, as this gives you better data to analyze budget implications. Due to COVID, a mid-
year budget adjustment might happen earlier than normal.

I am still evaluating the timeline of the mid-year review as the fiscal year just started and it’s too
early to make budgetary decisions without having additional data.

  22
 As you are aware, budget adjustments are only authorized by City Council. If any adjustments to
the library budget has to be made, it would be during the January council meeting. Please note, I
will make sure I work with you (the Community Services Director), the library’s manager (City
Librarian), and the Library Board of Trustees on the status of library’s budget before it goes to
the City Council.

Hopefully this provides you some additional insight and input on the budget process moving
forward.

MINUTES
  SPECIAL MEETING
  OF THE SAN MARINO LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES
  SEPTEMBER 28, 2020 – 7:30 A.M.
  VIA ZOOM TELECONFERENCE
CALL TO ORDER Chairperson Hollingsworth called the meeting to order at 7:31 A.M. via
the teleconferencing application, Zoom.
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE Chairperson Hollingsworth led the Pledge of Allegiance
ROLL CALL  PRESENT: Chairperson Liz Hollingsworth, Vice Chairperson Linda
  Mollno, Trustee Eldon Swanson, Trustee Steve Domier, Alternate
  Genevieve Chien, and Council Liaison Susan Jakubowski
  ABSENT: Trustee Lois Derry
  CITY STAFF PRESENT: Interim Community Services Director
  Josette Espinosa, City Librarian Irene McDermott, Management Analyst
  Robert Zubiate, and Acting City Clerk Amanda Merlo
PUBLIC COMMENTS
The following person(s) spoke:
NONE
APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  1. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  Trustee Domier moved to approve the minutes of the Library Board of Trustees meeting
  on Monday, August 24, 2020; seconded by Vice Chairperson Mollno. AYES: Chairperson
  Hollingsworth, Vice Chairperson Mollno, Trustee Domier, Alternate Chien. NOES:
  None.

BOARD OF TRUSTEES REPORTS
  1. CHAIRPERSON AND TRUSTEE REPORTS

  No reports were provided at this time.

  2. CRAIN ART GALLERY REPORT

  Vice Chairperson Mollno stated that the Crain Art Gallery is working on developing a
  virtual exhibit and the exhibit will be accessed through a video link posted on the Crowell
  Public Library’s website.

  City Librarian McDermott screen-shared the video for the Board of Trustees.

LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES – MINUTES  PAGE 1 OF 4
SPECIAL MEETING: SEPTEMBER 28, 2020
 LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES – MINUTES  PAGE 2 OF 4
SPECIAL MEETING: SEPTEMBER 28, 2020

  The Crain Art Gallery intends on also providing the links of other artists’ websites to give
  information about the artists about descriptions of their artwork.

  3. MARKETING AND PUBLICITY LIAISON REPORT

  Trustee Domier stated that there is a notion that the Library is doing a great deal of work
  that the public is not aware about. The goal for future marketing is reduce the amount of
  work required to know about the various programs and activities offered by the Library.
  Trustee Domier met with City Librarian McDermott on August 31, 2020 to identify
  marketing strategies and platforms, as well as to review the Library’s distribution lists and
  methods.

  Trustee Domier asked the Board members to engage more with the Library’s Facebook
  posts to further promote the Library.

  City Librarian McDermott summarize the Library’s current marketing efforts, including
  generating a newspaper article about passport collections.

  Trustee Domier suggested the use of banners and to be aware that residents are gradually
  modifying their use of social media which will eventually require new means of
  communication or engaging with the public. The key to marketing is to never rely on one
  source.

  Trustee Domier also summarized the City Council’s action pertaining to the renovation
  of the San Marino Center with a 3-2 vote in support of renovating the Center to match
  the Library’s exterior architecture.

  4. BUDGET AND CIP LIAISON REPORT

  Alternate Chien summarized the Budget and CIP Liaison meeting held with Interim
  Community Services Director Espinosa, City Librarian McDermott, and Analyst Zubiate
  on September 4, 2020. Alternate Chein emphasized that the goal is support Library staff
  and remain “in the black” in regards to expenditures. Staff reviewed the FY 20-21 budget
  and ideas for cost savings. There was emphasis to continue buying books and
  programming materials, to keep a visible profile in the community, and to understand the
  Library’s financial position during COVID-19. There was also discussion pertaining to the
  Library’s donation budget and the impacts on said budget during COVID-19.

  5. CITY COUNCIL LIAISON REPORT

  Councilmember Susan Jakubowski summarized the City Council’s action on September 9,
  2020 to approve the Board’s request to go from action minutes to summary minutes.
 LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES – MINUTES  PAGE 3 OF 4
SPECIAL MEETING: SEPTEMBER 28, 2020

  Councilmember Jakubowski also summarized the City Council’s action on September 25,
  2020 to concur on the City Manager’s hiring of Mr. Brian Haworth as the Community
  Services Director for the City of San Marino.

ADMINISTRATIVE BUSINESS
  1. CITY LIBRARIAN’S REPORT

  City Librarian McDermott presented the staff report.

  Vice Chairperson Mollno inquired about the Crowell Public Library serving as a voting
  center to which Acting City Clerk Merlo stated a ballot box was placed in front of City
  Hall. The Library could not serve as a voting center as it was not large enough to
  accommodate physical distancing requirements.

  Chairperson Hollingsworth inquired about passport collections to which City Librarian
  McDermott stated passport appointments are being quickly filled and revenues should
  increase substantially for the Library.

  2. MANAGEMENT ANALYST’S REPORT

  Analyst Zubiate presented the staff report. Analyst Zubiate reported that the Board’s
  request to get funding again for the Barth Community Room Audio/Visual upgrade was
  pushed from the September 25, 2020 Council meeting to the October 14, 2020 Council
  meeting.

  Chairperson Hollingsworth inquired about the new statistics report format to which
  Analyst Zubiate stated a meeting would be scheduled with the Budget Liaisons to review
  that project.

CONTINUED BUSINESS
  1. UPDATE ON THE LIBRARY’S REVENUES IN RESPONSE TO COVID-19

  Analyst Zubiate provided a summary on the memorandum received from Finance
  Director Paul Chung in relation to the City’s plan to address any financial issues that may
  stem from COVID-19.

  Chairperson Hollingsworth advised City Librarian McDermott to focus spending on
  children’s books and materials, and to identify a budget that would allow the Library to
  meet the demands of the community, particularly during COVID-19. Analyst Zubiate
  emphasized there were underspent General Fund accounts that could be evaluated to be
  potentially spent towards children’s books and materials in lieu of resorting to spending
  from the restricted donations reserves.
 LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES  -MINUTES  PAGE 4 OF 4
SPECIAL MEETING: SEPTEMBER 28, 2020

  2, DISCUSSION OF MAINTENANCE SCHEDULE FOR THE CROWELL
  PUBLIC LIBRARY

  Chairperson Hollingsworth continued this item to a date when Parks & Public Works
  Director Michael Throne is able to participate in this discussion.

NE\tr BUSINESS
  I. REVIEW OF THE BROWN ACT
  City Librarian McDermott stated a State of California Brown Act summary document was
  included in the agenda packet for the Board's review.

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS OR PUBLIC WRITINGS DISTRIBUTED
There were no public writings distributed.

PUBLIC COMMENTS
There were no public comments at this time.

ADJOURNMENT
Chairperson Hollingsworth adjourned the meeting at 8:16 A.M. to a Special Meeting on
MONDAY, OCTOBER 26, 2020 AT 7:30 A.M. to be conducted via Zoom teleconference.

  ROB T ZUBIATE
  MANAGEMENT ANALYST
